solution: Multiply the two numbers and use \(i^{2} = -1\). \((5i)\left(-\frac{3}{5}i\right) = -\frac{15}{5}\,i^{2} = -3i^{2} = -3(-1) = 3\). In the form \(a + ib\), the number is \(3 + i0\).

Since \(i^{4} = 1\), we may multiply by \(i^{40} = 1\) to clear the negative exponent: \(i^{-39} = i^{-39}\cdot i^{40} = i^{1} = i\). (Check: \(i^{39} = i^{36}\cdot i^{3} = -i\), and \((-i)(i) = -i^{2} = 1\), so the reciprocal of \(i^{39}\) is indeed \(i\).) In the form \(a + ib\), the number is \(0 + i\).
Expand both products and use \(i^{2} = -1\). \(3(7 + i7) = 21 + 21i\) and \(i(7 + i7) = 7i + 7i^{2} = -7 + 7i\). Adding, \((21 - 7) + (21 + 7)i = 14 + 28i\). Hence the number is \(14 + 28i\).
Subtract real and imaginary parts separately. \((1 - i) - (-1 + i6) = (1 - (-1)) + (-1 - 6)i = 2 - 7i\). Hence the number is \(2 - 7i\).

Subtract real and imaginary parts separately. Real part: \(\frac{1}{5} - 4 = \frac{1 - 20}{5} = -\frac{19}{5}\). Imaginary part: \(\frac{2}{5} - \frac{5}{2} = \frac{4 - 25}{10} = -\frac{21}{10}\). Hence the number is \(-\frac{19}{5} - i\,\frac{21}{10}\).

Combine real and imaginary parts separately. Real part: \(\frac{1}{3} + 4 - \left(-\frac{4}{3}\right) = \frac{1}{3} + \frac{4}{3} + 4 = \frac{5}{3} + 4 = \frac{17}{3}\). Imaginary part: \(\frac{7}{3} + \frac{1}{3} - 1 = \frac{8}{3} - 1 = \frac{5}{3}\). Hence the number is \(\frac{17}{3} + i\,\frac{5}{3}\).
Square first, then square again. \((1 - i)^{2} = 1 - 2i + i^{2} = 1 - 2i - 1 = -2i\). Therefore \((1 - i)^{4} = (-2i)^{2} = 4i^{2} = -4\). In the form \(a + ib\), the number is \(-4 + i0\).

Use \((a + b)^{3} = a^{3} + 3a^{2}b + 3ab^{2} + b^{3}\) with \(a = \frac{1}{3}\), \(b = 3i\). Then \(a^{3} = \frac{1}{27}\), \(3a^{2}b = 3\cdot\frac{1}{9}\cdot 3i = i\), \(3ab^{2} = 3\cdot\frac{1}{3}\cdot 9i^{2} = -9\), and \(b^{3} = 27i^{3} = -27i\). Collecting, the real part is \(\frac{1}{27} - 9 = \frac{1 - 243}{27} = -\frac{242}{27}\) and the imaginary part is \(1 - 27 = -26\). Hence the number is \(-\frac{242}{27} - 26i\).

Write \(\left(-2 - \frac{1}{3}i\right)^{3} = -\left(2 + \frac{1}{3}i\right)^{3}\) and expand with \(a = 2\), \(b = \frac{i}{3}\): \(a^{3} = 8\), \(3a^{2}b = 3\cdot 4\cdot\frac{i}{3} = 4i\), \(3ab^{2} = 6\cdot\frac{i^{2}}{9} = -\frac{2}{3}\), \(b^{3} = \frac{i^{3}}{27} = -\frac{i}{27}\). So \(\left(2 + \frac{1}{3}i\right)^{3} = \left(8 - \frac{2}{3}\right) + \left(4 - \frac{1}{27}\right)i = \frac{22}{3} + \frac{107}{27}i\). Changing sign, the number is \(-\frac{22}{3} - \frac{107}{27}i\).

The multiplicative inverse of \(z\) is \(z^{-1} = \frac{\overline{z}}{|z|^{2}}\). Here \(\overline{z} = 4 + 3i\) and \(|z|^{2} = 4^{2} + (-3)^{2} = 25\). Hence \((4 - 3i)^{-1} = \frac{4 + 3i}{25} = \frac{4}{25} + \frac{3}{25}i\). Check: \((4 - 3i)\left(\frac{4 + 3i}{25}\right) = \frac{16 + 9}{25} = 1\). The multiplicative inverse is \(\frac{4}{25} + \frac{3}{25}i\).

Use \(z^{-1} = \frac{\overline{z}}{|z|^{2}}\) with \(z = -i\): \(\overline{z} = i\) and \(|z|^{2} = 1\). Hence \((-i)^{-1} = i\). Check: \((-i)(i) = -i^{2} = 1\). The multiplicative inverse is \(i\), i.e. \(0 + i\).

The numerator is a difference of squares: \((3 + i\sqrt{5})(3 - i\sqrt{5}) = 3^{2} - (i\sqrt{5})^{2} = 9 + 5 = 14\). The denominator is \((\sqrt{3} + \sqrt{2}\,i) - (\sqrt{3} - i\sqrt{2}) = 2\sqrt{2}\,i\). So the expression equals \(\frac{14}{2\sqrt{2}\,i} = \frac{7}{\sqrt{2}\,i}\). Multiplying numerator and denominator by \(i\) and using \(i^{2} = -1\), \(\frac{7i}{\sqrt{2}\,i^{2}} = -\frac{7}{\sqrt{2}}i = -\frac{7\sqrt{2}}{2}i\). Hence the number is \(0 - \frac{7\sqrt{2}}{2}i\).

solution: Squaring the given relation, \((x - iy)^{2} = \frac{a - ib}{c - id}\). Take moduli of both sides and use \(|z_{1}/z_{2}| = |z_{1}|/|z_{2}|\) and \(|z^{2}| = |z|^{2}\): \(|x - iy|^{2} = \frac{|a - ib|}{|c - id|}\), that is \(x^{2} + y^{2} = \frac{\sqrt{a^{2} + b^{2}}}{\sqrt{c^{2} + d^{2}}}\). Squaring once more gives \(\left(x^{2} + y^{2}\right)^{2} = \frac{a^{2} + b^{2}}{c^{2} + d^{2}}\), as required.

Compute numerator and denominator. \(z_{1} + z_{2} + 1 = (2 - i) + (1 + i) + 1 = 4\), and \(z_{1} - z_{2} + 1 = (2 - i) - (1 + i) + 1 = 2 - 2i\). Then \(\left|\frac{4}{2 - 2i}\right| = \frac{|4|}{|2 - 2i|} = \frac{4}{\sqrt{4 + 4}} = \frac{4}{2\sqrt{2}} = \sqrt{2}\). Hence the required modulus is \(\sqrt{2}\).

Note that \(a^{2} + b^{2} = |a + ib|^{2}\). Taking the modulus of the given relation, \(|a + ib| = \frac{|x + i|^{2}}{|2x^{2} + 1|} = \frac{x^{2} + 1}{2x^{2} + 1}\), since \(|x + i| = \sqrt{x^{2} + 1}\) and \(2x^{2} + 1 > 0\) is real. Squaring, \(a^{2} + b^{2} = \frac{(x^{2} + 1)^{2}}{\left(2x^{2} + 1\right)^{2}}\), as required.

For any complex number, \(z\overline{z} = |z|^{2}\), which is real. Here \(z_{1}\overline{z}_{1} = |2 - i|^{2} = 2^{2} + (-1)^{2} = 5\), so \(\frac{1}{z_{1}\overline{z}_{1}} = \frac{1}{5}\), a real number. Its imaginary part is therefore \(0\). Hence \(\mathrm{Im}\left(\frac{1}{z_{1}\overline{z}_{1}}\right) = 0\).

The conjugate of \(-6 - 24i\) is \(-6 + 24i\), so we need \((x - iy)(3 + 5i) = -6 + 24i\). Expanding the left side, \(3x + 5xi - 3iy - 5i^{2}y = (3x + 5y) + i(5x - 3y)\). Equating real and imaginary parts, \(3x + 5y = -6\) and \(5x - 3y = 24\). Multiplying the first by \(3\), the second by \(5\) and adding gives \(34x = 102\), so \(x = 3\); then \(9 + 5y = -6\) gives \(y = -3\). Hence \(x = 3\) and \(y = -3\).

Simplify each fraction: \(\frac{1 + i}{1 - i} = \frac{(1 + i)^{2}}{(1 - i)(1 + i)} = \frac{2i}{2} = i\), and similarly \(\frac{1 - i}{1 + i} = \frac{(1 - i)^{2}}{2} = \frac{-2i}{2} = -i\). So the expression equals \(i - (-i) = 2i\), whose modulus is \(|2i| = 2\). Hence the modulus is \(2\).

Expand the cube: \((x + iy)^{3} = x^{3} + 3x^{2}(iy) + 3x(iy)^{2} + (iy)^{3} = \left(x^{3} - 3xy^{2}\right) + i\left(3x^{2}y - y^{3}\right)\). Comparing with \(u + iv\) gives \(u = x^{3} - 3xy^{2}\) and \(v = 3x^{2}y - y^{3}\). Therefore \(\frac{u}{x} = x^{2} - 3y^{2}\) and \(\frac{v}{y} = 3x^{2} - y^{2}\), so \(\frac{u}{x} + \frac{v}{y} = 4x^{2} - 4y^{2} = 4\left(x^{2} - y^{2}\right)\), as required.

Since \(|\beta| = 1\), we have \(\beta\overline{\beta} = |\beta|^{2} = 1\). Use this to rewrite the denominator: \(1 - \overline{\alpha}\beta = \beta\overline{\beta} - \overline{\alpha}\beta = \beta\left(\overline{\beta} - \overline{\alpha}\right) = \beta\,\overline{\left(\beta - \alpha\right)}\). Taking moduli, \(\left|1 - \overline{\alpha}\beta\right| = |\beta|\,\left|\overline{\beta - \alpha}\right| = |\beta - \alpha|\). Since \(\alpha \ne \beta\), this is non-zero, so \(\left|\frac{\beta - \alpha}{1 - \overline{\alpha}\beta}\right| = \frac{|\beta - \alpha|}{|\beta - \alpha|} = 1\). Hence the value is \(1\).

Here \(|1 - i| = \sqrt{1^{2} + (-1)^{2}} = \sqrt{2}\), so the equation becomes \(\left(\sqrt{2}\right)^{x} = 2^{x}\), i.e. \(2^{x/2} = 2^{x}\). Since the bases are equal and the base is not \(1\), the exponents must agree: \(\frac{x}{2} = x\), giving \(x = 0\). The only solution is \(x = 0\), which is excluded, so there is no non-zero integral solution. Hence the number of non-zero integral solutions is \(0\).

Take the modulus of both sides and use \(|z_{1}z_{2}| = |z_{1}||z_{2}|\): \(|a + ib|\,|c + id|\,|e + if|\,|g + ih| = |\mathrm{A} + i\mathrm{B}|\). Now square both sides, using \(|p + iq|^{2} = p^{2} + q^{2}\): \(\left(a^{2} + b^{2}\right)\left(c^{2} + d^{2}\right)\left(e^{2} + f^{2}\right)\left(g^{2} + h^{2}\right) = \mathrm{A}^{2} + \mathrm{B}^{2}\), as required.

Simplify the base: \(\frac{1 + i}{1 - i} = \frac{(1 + i)^{2}}{(1 - i)(1 + i)} = \frac{2i}{2} = i\). The equation becomes \(i^{m} = 1\), and since the powers of \(i\) cycle as \(i, -1, -i, 1\), we need \(m\) to be a multiple of \(4\). The least positive such value is \(m = 4\).
